verdict: F — Gentle DD insufficient. MDD 40.3% (still <45% but barely). CAGR 10.2% slightly better than ddA/B but SR 0.546 is worst. FF5 alpha +3.39% weakest. Worst of three variants.

gate1_performance.detail: MDD 40.3% — barely under 45% gate, fragile. CAGR 10.2% slightly better than ddA/B (the gentle brake preserves more upside). But SR 0.546 is virtually identical to base (0.547) — the DD overlay adds no risk-adjusted value. Worst month -15% still bad.

gate3_role_honesty.detail: Grade F — no role assignment. The gentle DD does not fix the fundamental problem.

gate4_statistical.detail: OOS 0.129 is worst of three — most alpha leaks through gentle DD. Alpha trend 0.227 higher than ddA/B (less compression = more variance = more apparent trend). This is not genuine improvement.

gate5_ff5.detail: FF5 alpha +3.39%/yr (t=0.736). Survival rate only 51.3% — worst of three. Higher R^2 (0.456) means more of the variance is explained by factors = less unexplained alpha. Gentle DD paradoxically loses more alpha because it allows bigger drawdowns (higher systematic exposure during crashes = higher factor beta loading).

comparison_note: Worst of three variants on every risk-adjusted metric. Gentle DD threshold is insufficient — it neither controls MDD well nor preserves alpha. The only advantage is slightly higher CAGR (10.2% vs 9.5%) but at cost of 40% MDD.
promotion_reason: Grade F. SR unchanged from base. MDD barely under 45%. OOS worst of three.
